title: The Measure of a Melusine
subtitle: The little snakes eagerly flick their tongues at you, warm like another burning heart.

trails.title: The Story of Cepheus
trails.description: She doesn't seem like the storytelling type, but a long, long time ago ...

content.text:
Cepheus learned a wonderful way to live.

Always keep your eyes on the future. Keep walking forward. It believed that was the right thing to do.

Cepheus moved quickly. And so, it fell hard. After that, it donned a metal shell.

Inside that metal shell, the ghost of Cepheus witnessed countless beautiful moments—

A near-eternal hearth being lit. Man-made stars launched into the sky. Earth's songs reaching beyond the Solar System.

But it all vanished in the rain. Its dreams ended.

And Cepheus felt regret for the first time. It realized, perhaps, that it didn't really know how to live after all.

Cepheus believed itself to be a guiding pointer for millennia to come, leading the way for ten thousand years. But in truth, it realized it didn't even understand the road to the next hundred years. It couldn't even light the paths of the Southern Hemisphere.

What happened to Cepheus afterward? It returned to the space base and continued its research for the sake of those still living.

Yes. I am Cepheus.

items.text: Pointer is visibly winded. Her vehicle couldn't drive into the inner perimeter of the launch bay, so she had to run the last stretch.
But she has to make the most of her time. She came back to say what needed to be said.
Hissabeth speaks first.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Are you alright? You look like you haven't slept in days.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: How many times have I told you that research requires a healthy body and mind? You need sleep.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: I'm ... here for ...

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Just so you know, I've got no time to help with whatever you're working on, and we're finishing this project, no matter what you say.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Oh, let me guess. You're here for the car? Yes, I've used it a few times, took the team out to the mine, didn't break anything or get any tickets, but the tank's dry.
Her every theory misses the mark.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: It's not about any of that!

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Then you should have come earlier—days earlier, not today.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: The "Storm" is due to come in a couple hours. You won't make it to the Northern Branch.
Pointer falls silent for a moment instead, adjusting her breath.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: I'm here to settle your affairs. We need to secure your records in case you don't make it, and to see if the work you've done is actually worth your lives.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Just so you know, if you don't survive, I'm going to finish our teleport disk and claim all the credit. Maybe I'll write a dissertation on it. I'll call it "Pointer's Teleport Disk," and you'll all just be a footnote, an "et al." in the citations.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: You know I'm not bluffing.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Cool, whatever, Pointer. Just don't forget to tell me the results. Maybe send them to me via Ouija board.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Are you being serious?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Aren't you? Or are you trying to be funny now? I really can't tell.
The casual air she fought to maintain finally breaks.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: I'm just sick of eating instant noodles without the veggie packets!

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: But more than that, I'm sick of you and your attitude!

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: All you do is joke around!

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: If veggies matter that much to a stupid bowl of noodles, how could you think your lives matter any less to me?!

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: You want to treat your lives like a cosmic joke? Like your deaths won't matter. Well, they will to the ones you leave behind.
After giving up on controlling her volume and her thoughts, she catches a different expression on Hissabeth's face.
Guilt, sadness, shock? None of the above.
She has simply put away her smile.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: I see your point.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Luckily, I've already made a copy of everything on this data card.
A brighter, more genuine smile appears.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: I've been wondering who I should trust with it. It's not 100% safe to send back through the teleportation ritual.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: It's good to have you back.
The thin card is handed to her again.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: The editing isn't done. Han Zhang—yeah, I can remember his name now—I didn't have time to finish his part.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: But who has time to edit a suicide note?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: The only thing that matters is that it's in the hands of someone who will take it seriously.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Take it and go. You can still make it back.
The data card feels faintly warm. It must have been in her pocket the entire time.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: *sigh* Forget it. You already told me the car's out of gas.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: So, I'll be your witness.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: You sure you wanna die with us, after all?
Pointer doesn't respond. She just takes a step forward.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Call it a fool's wish, but I'm hoping no one is ever going to need to see this.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Catch me up to speed, what's the status of the project?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: We've managed to refine the teleportation to pinpoint a fixed position, but there are still some serious side effects: dizziness, nausea, like the world's worst case of carsickness.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: It'll have to suffice for now. I think I can work that out after I finish reading your progress.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Cool, I'll look forward to that.
She points to the door.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Your office should be the same as you left it, besides a layer of dust. Be grateful though. You should see the state of mine.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Oh, and don't activate the teleportation anywhere around here. If it takes out the single critical component, we'll be screwed completely.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Like I don't know.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: You need a hand here? I can help.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: I thought we already figured out our roles? You need to stay at a safe distance to protect the data.
She can't quite tell if there's mockery in her words.
But she doesn't need to get to the bottom of it. Language is vague and fleeting. Words lose meaning the moment they're spoken.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: That's it.
Before turning around, she pauses and tucks her hair behind her ear.
Her data ports and mechanical components reflect in the sterile light of the lab.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Ha. I always thought I wasn't able to act against my safety programming.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Yet here we are.
Another rare expression on Hissabeth's face. Pointer's database logs it as a surprise, but the emotion doesn't linger long.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Do you have a sense of taste?
Pointer once thought her facial expression metrics could no longer be thrown off by strange inputs. Yet her smile is off its index by 0.35 degrees.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Yeah. I was designed to simulate all aspects of life.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Really? But whose life? Who decided whether it should be a human's or arcanist's life?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: I suppose you are probably another Awakened arcanist, like Ulrich and Madam Lucy.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Not exactly. But the details can wait.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: I thought you would be more encouraging at such a vital moment. Guess my prediction matrix is not quite as perfect as I've let on.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: I am encouraging you. I'm trying to prove your existence matters.
Faced with Hissabeth tilting her head in confusion, Pointer's smile registers even higher.
Since leaving the Cosmodrome, this is the lightest she's felt.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Well, I should go. Take care.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Time for another double-check. Everything needs to be flawless.
This hallway is etched into Pointer's memory. She could navigate it without any sensors.
As she turns, Hissabeth calls out to her.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Pointer!

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: You know, I should have mentioned something before, something I wanted you to see.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: There are Melusine statues everywhere in Lusignan!

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: I left a long time ago, but they should still be there. Even the "Storm" can't wash them away. They've been there for ages!

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Go take a look if you ever get the time!

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: I don't think Laplace would cover that as a scientific excursion.
She doesn't stop or turn back, but gives Hissabeth a gesture.
The name is Pointer. Researcher in LSCC Plesetsk Branch. Former team member on the Space Monitor Project.
The reason I quit? Because someone must be prepared for the worst-case scenario.
And because I was tired of freeze-dried noodles.
Two other friends have come to say a quiet goodbye.
Though they can't quite exchange wishes through speech, they still try.
Voyager struggles to control the marker, but she writes, and Kiperina waits patiently.
The markings on her palm form a complex, indecipherable pattern—precise in geometry, yet unreadable in meaning.

items.speaker: Voyager
items.text: Alia. Come home.
The little astronaut pulls her focus away from the pattern. She takes a few deep breaths, just to be sure she heard it right.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: That was three whole words!

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Maybe once you learn a few more, you can tell me where you're really from.
There's a shift of weight on her shoe.
Kiperina lowers her head. A familiar little snake looks back up at her.

items.speaker: Snake VIII
items.text: My sister sent me to tell you it's time.

items.speaker: Snake VIII
items.text: And that you shouldn't be afraid. You'll make one cool astronaut, ask any of us.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: I'm not afraid.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: When I return, remind me to show you Natalya's famous jam recipe.
Maybe the pattern really does hold some kind of magic, or maybe it's just the feeling of looking forward to the future.
But either way, her steps feel lighter.
Cabin, Spacecraft

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Final diagnostics completed.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: We're clear for launch in T-minus one minute.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Is there anything else I have to remember?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Yes: keep breathing.

items.speaker: Kiperina
items.text: Really, a joke now? Or are you serious?

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: It can be both things.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Now get ready, and have a safe flight.
The transmission ends. Hissabeth scans each face in the launch bay, the confidence in her teammates putting her at ease.
She knows that everyone here is committed to the end. She places her hand on the button.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Three.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Two.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: One.

items.speaker: Hissabeth
items.text: Ignition.
